headline: GOLD SHATTERS $4,000 FLOOR, SILVER CRATERS 6.5% IN ONE SESSION — STRONGEST DOLLAR IN A YEAR DEEPENS POST-WARSH FED SELLOFF
snippet: Gold broke decisively below $4,000 per ounce on June 24 while silver sank 6.5% in a single session as the U.S. dollar surged to a one-year high and Treasury yields held near 4.4% — the steepest single-week precious metals selloff since January's all-time highs — as markets priced in an 80% chance of a December Fed rate hike following new Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish June policy meeting. A partial rebound toward $4,036 on June 26 after in-line PCE data has not reversed the trend: gold remains down roughly 20% from its January record and silver nearly 53% below its peak.

headline: EQUINOX + ORLA SET JULY 22 VOTE ON US$18.5B NORTH AMERICAN GOLD MERGER — COMBINED 1.1 MILLION OZ/YR FROM 3 CORNERSTONE CANADIAN MINES
snippet: Equinox Gold (TSX:EQX) mailed proxy materials June 23 for a July 22 special meeting to approve its at-market all-share combination with Orla Mining (TSX:ORLA), creating a US$18.5 billion North American senior gold producer with combined expected 2026 production of 1.1 million ounces from the Greenstone, Valentine, and Musselwhite mines in Canada. Both boards unanimously recommend voting FOR; court approval and Canadian and Mexican competition clearances remain outstanding with Q3 2026 close targeted.

headline: GOLDMAN SACHS SLASHES GOLD TARGET $500 TO $4,900 — FED CUTS PUSHED TO JUNE 2027, HIKE SCENARIO PUTS GOLD AT $4,400
snippet: Goldman Sachs analysts cut their year-end gold price target from $5,400 to $4,900 on June 24, citing the Fed's first rate cut being pushed to June 2027 under Chair Kevin Warsh — Goldman's own model puts each 50bp of delayed easing at roughly $120/oz of lost support. The bank now puts downside risk at $4,400 if the Fed actually hikes rates, placing Goldman $1,100 below JPMorgan's $6,000/oz Q4 forecast and opening the widest inter-bank gold outlook gap of the current bull cycle.

headline: HEMLO MINING BOOSTS M&I GOLD 34% TO 4.84M OZ — UNDERGROUND +40% TO 2.83M OZ AT 3.53 g/t AS 130,000m PROGRAM 35% DONE (TSX:HMMC)
snippet: Hemlo Mining Corp. (TSX:HMMC) released an updated Mineral Resource Estimate on June 25 for its Hemlo Gold Mine near Marathon, Ontario: total M+I resources reached 4.84 million ounces — up 1.2 million ounces from the 2025 technical report — led by a 40% jump in underground M+I to 2.83 million ounces at 3.53 g/t Au and a 25% increase in open-pit resources to 2.01 million ounces. The estimate incorporates 45,000 metres of a 130,000-metre 2026 drill program focused on resource conversion at a mine already in active development.

headline: NUVAU DRILLS 5.28 g/t AU OVER 6.1m AT THUNDERMINE — FIRST HOLE AT MATAGAMI VMS TARGET IN 40 YEARS CONFIRMS GOLD-BEARING SYSTEM (TSXV:NMC)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Nuvau Minerals Inc. (TSXV:NMC)
snippet: Nuvau Minerals (TSXV:NMC) announced June 26 the first drill results from its Thundermine target in Quebec's Matagami Mining Camp — the first hole drilled at this target in nearly four decades — returning 5.28 g/t gold over 6.1 metres including 7.22 g/t over 3.1 metres, alongside VMS-style alteration wider than historical shallow drilling indicated. CEO Christina McCarthy noted the system's width is significantly broader than historical intercepts, suggesting potential for meaningful continuity at depth within a camp already hosting Nuvau's active 17,500-metre program.

headline: TALISKER FILES NI 43-101 ON BRALORNE'S 3.15M OZ INFERRED — HIGH-GRADE BC UNDERGROUND RESOURCE NOW CLEARED FOR ECONOMIC STUDIES (TSX:TSK)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Talisker Resources Ltd. (TSX:TSK)
snippet: Talisker Resources (TSX:TSK) filed its NI 43-101 technical report on June 26 with SEDAR+, formally certifying the Bralorne Gold Project's 2026 Mineral Resource Estimate — independently prepared by SGS Canada — which includes 3.15 million inferred ounces of gold alongside high-grade Measured and Indicated ounces at 8.91 g/t Au, positioning Bralorne as one of British Columbia's highest-grade major gold resources. The formal certification is the milestone that allows PEA engineers and institutional investors to rely on the resource for preliminary economic assessments.

headline: NEXMETALS UPGRADES SELKIRK COPPER 63% TO 1.1B LBS CuEq INDICATED — STRIP RATIO DROPS TO 1.02:1, COBALT AND PGE NOW PAYABLE (TSXV:NEXM)
snippet: NexMetals Mining Corp. (TSXV:NEXM) published a June 24 MRE update for its Selkirk Project in Botswana — 78.2 million tonnes at 0.66% CuEq for 1.1 billion pounds indicated, a 63% increase in contained metal — after re-assaying and twin-drilling converted resources from Inferred to Indicated and added cobalt, silver, and gold as newly payable metals. The strip ratio fell to 1.02:1 from 1.65:1, one of the lowest for any copper development project globally, as Selkirk advances toward construction-stage readiness alongside NexMetals' flagship Selebi project.

headline: FARADAY COMPLETES PHASE IV AT COPPER CREEK: OPEN-PIT DEFINITION DONE, NEW OXIDE ZONE FOUND EAST OF COPPER GIANT — SAN MANUEL DEAL PENDING (TSX:FDY)
snippet: Faraday Copper Corp. (TSX:FDY) reported June 24 completion of its Phase IV drill program at the Copper Creek Project in Arizona, fulfilling the open-pit resource definition mandate and identifying a new oxide copper zone east of Copper Giant that adds incremental resource potential. Drilling has been suspended as of June 20 and will resume in fall 2026 pending close of the proposed San Manuel copper mine acquisition — a transaction that would convert Faraday from a development-stage junior into an active Arizona copper producer.

headline: GEORGIA JOINS CENTRAL BANK GOLD RUSH — CAUCASUS NATION ADDS BULLION AS DEDOLLARIZATION SPREADS TO FORMER SOVIET STATES
snippet: The Republic of Georgia announced an expansion of its central bank gold reserves on June 23, joining a broad wave of emerging market and post-Soviet states diversifying away from U.S. dollar-denominated assets as the dollar surges to a one-year high. The development adds to what GoldSeek analysts describe as a structural floor of 1,000+ tonnes annual central bank buying that makes gold's current correction qualitatively different from pre-2020 pullbacks — persistent sovereign physical demand even as Western paper gold positioning retreats.

headline: CHINA GOLD IMPORTS HIT TWO-YEAR HIGH IN MAY — EASTERN PHYSICAL DEMAND SURGES AS WESTERN INSTITUTIONS EXIT ON FED HAWKISHNESS
snippet: Chinese gold imports reached a two-year high in May 2026 as retail and central bank demand persisted through the correction despite a 20% pullback from January's all-time high, according to a June 23 Money Metals analysis republished on GoldSeek. The surge highlights gold's bifurcated market: Western institutional outflows triggered by Fed hawkishness are occurring simultaneously with record Eastern physical accumulation — a divergence historically resolved when Western capital re-enters and finds the physical floor already in place.

headline: GLEASON: REAL FORT KNOX AUDIT WOULD TAKE 30 YEARS — PURITY PROBLEMS AND POTENTIAL SWAP ENCUMBRANCES UNDERCUT DOLLAR RESERVE CLAIM
snippet: Money Metals CEO Stefan Gleason argued in a June 23 commentary that a genuine Fort Knox audit would require decades to complete, citing inadequate historical inventory procedures, large quantities of below-standard-purity gold requiring 20–30 years of market-neutral refining, and potential encumbrances through undisclosed swaps and leases not visible on Treasury's official ledger. Gleason frames the audit debate as the defining test of whether the dollar's reserve status rests on real physical gold — and argues mainstream media coverage has grossly underestimated the complexity and stakes.

headline: KITCO ANALYST: NEW RISKS BUILDING FAST — HAWKISH WARSH AND SURGING DOLLAR COULD PUSH PRECIOUS METALS CORRECTION DEEPER BEFORE BOTTOM
snippet: A June 23 Kitco opinion piece warned that gold and silver face a compounding set of new downside risks not present at the January all-time highs — primarily Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's unexpectedly hawkish stance and a dollar at its strongest in over a year — and argued the current corrective phase may need to run deeper before reversing rather than offering an immediate buy-the-dip entry. The analysis cautions investors against treating the correction as over until clearer signals emerge from the Fed's rate trajectory.
